description: MOEA/D solves a problem with several objectives by splitting it into many single-objective subproblems (*decomposition*). Each subproblem has a weight vector and a scalarising function that turns the objective vector into one cost: a weighted sum, the Tchebycheff distance to the *ideal point* (the best value seen for each objective), or penalty-based boundary intersection (PBI). Subproblems with close weight vectors are *neighbours*: a child is bred from two parents of the neighbourhood (with probability `δ`, otherwise of the whole population), and it replaces at most `n_r` members of that pool that it solves at least as well on their own subproblem, with lower constraint violation first. The result approximates the *Pareto front*, the set of trade-offs where no objective can improve without another getting worse. It has no convergence guarantee; use it when a set of weight vectors can cover the front, for example from Das-Dennis points.

papers.title: MOEA/D: A Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Decomposition
